title: apple: rebind brcmfmac across suspend
author: teomurgi
body:
## Problem

On Macs whose Wi-Fi is driven by `brcmfmac` (BCM4350 and relatives), a long suspend wedges the Broadcom firmware. After wake the kernel logs `brcmf_msgbuf_query_dcmd: Timeout on response for query command` for every request, NetworkManager sees `do-change-link: failure 5 (Input/output error)`, and the interface never recovers — only a reboot brings Wi-Fi back. Short suspends (seconds) resume fine; the failure shows up after hours asleep.

Observed on a MacBook10,1 (BCM4350, `14e4:43a3`): suspended 16:53, resumed 19:55, firmware dead from the first msgbuf command after wake.

## Fix

A `systemd/system-sleep` hook unbinds the Wi-Fi PCI device from `brcmfmac` before sleep and rebinds it after wake, forcing a clean firmware reload. NetworkManager then sees a fresh interface and reconnects on its own (~seconds after wake). Devices unbound at `pre` are recorded under `/run` and only those are rebound at `post`; a `post` with no matching `pre` is a no-op.

## Gating

Mirrors `fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh`: T2 Macs via the T2 PCI ID, older Macs via the `brcmfmac` PCI IDs from `brcm_hw_ids.h`. Hardware brcmfmac doesn't drive is left alone.

## Rollout

- New installs: `install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-suspend.sh` runs from `install/hardware/all.sh`.
- Existing installs: migration installs the hook. No reboot needed — systemd-sleep runs every executable in `system-sleep` on the next suspend. Idempotent: an identical hook is left untouched, a locally modified one is refreshed.

## Tests

`test/shell.d/brcmfmac-suspend-test.sh` (13 assertions): hardware gating for the leaf and migration, idempotency, refresh of a modified hook, and the hook's own pre/post/no-op behavior against a stub sysfs. `brcmfmac-supplicant-test.sh` and `system-sleep-ownership-migration-test.sh` still pass.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+# Rebind the Broadcom Wi-Fi device around system sleep. The brcmfmac firmware
+# on these parts does not reliably survive a long suspend: after wake it stops
+# answering msgbuf commands (the kernel logs "Timeout on response for query
+# command" for every request), the interface never recovers, and only a reboot
+# brings Wi-Fi back. Unbinding before sleep and rebinding after wake forces the
+# firmware to reload cleanly, so NetworkManager sees a fresh interface and
+# reconnects on its own.
+
+driver=/sys/bus/pci/drivers/brcmfmac
+state_file=${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_SLEEP_STATE:-/run/omarchy-brcmfmac-sleep}
+
+case "$1" in
+  pre)
+    : > "$state_file"
+    for bound in "$driver"/0000:*; do
+      [[ -L $bound ]] || continue
+      device=$(basename "$bound")
+      echo "$device" > "$driver/unbind" 2>/dev/null && echo "$device" >> "$state_file"
+    done
+    ;;
+  post)
+    [[ -f $state_file ]] || exit 0
+    while read -r device; do
+      echo "$device" > "$driver/bind" 2>/dev/null || true
+    done < "$state_file"
+    rm -f "$state_file"
+    ;;
+esac

@@ -0,0 +1,19 @@
+# Apple Macs with Broadcom Wi-Fi driven by brcmfmac lose Wi-Fi after a long
+# suspend: the firmware stops answering commands on wake and the interface
+# never recovers without a reboot. A system-sleep hook that rebinds the device
+# across sleep reloads the firmware cleanly.
+#
+# The hardware gate mirrors fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh: T2 Macs are detected by
+# the T2 PCI ID, older Macs by the brcmfmac PCI IDs from brcm_hw_ids.h. Only
+# machines whose Wi-Fi brcmfmac actually drives get the hook.
+sys_vendor="$(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor 2>/dev/null || true)"
+
+if lspci -nn | grep "106b:180[12]" >/dev/null ||
+  { [[ $sys_vendor == Apple* ]] &&
+    lspci -nn | grep -E "14e4:(43ba|43bb|43bc|43a3|43dc|4464|4488|4425|4433)" >/dev/null; }; then
+  echo "Detected a Mac with Broadcom Wi-Fi; rebinding brcmfmac across suspend"
+
+  sudo install -Dm 0755 -o root -g root \
+    "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/systemd/system-sleep/rebind-brcmfmac" \
+    /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/rebind-brcmfmac
+fi

@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+echo "Rebind Broadcom Wi-Fi across suspend on Macs with brcmfmac"
+
+# The install-time hook only reaches machines set up after it shipped, so an
+# existing install on one still loses Wi-Fi after a long suspend. See
+# install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-suspend.sh for the failure it fixes and
+# for where this list of brcmfmac PCI IDs comes from.
+dmi_vendor="${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_DMI_VENDOR:-/sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor}"
+hook="${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_SLEEP_HOOK:-/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/rebind-brcmfmac}"
+
+sys_vendor="$(cat "$dmi_vendor" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+
+if ! lspci -nn | grep "106b:180[12]" >/dev/null &&
+  ! { [[ $sys_vendor == Apple* ]] &&
+    lspci -nn | grep -E "14e4:(43ba|43bb|43bc|43a3|43dc|4464|4488|4425|4433)" >/dev/null; }; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# Idempotent: a hook identical to the source is already the fix.
+if [[ -f $hook ]] && /usr/bin/cmp -s "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/systemd/system-sleep/rebind-brcmfmac" "$hook"; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+sudo /usr/bin/mkdir -p "$(dirname "$hook")"
+sudo /usr/bin/install -m 0755 -o root -g root \
+  "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/systemd/system-sleep/rebind-brcmfmac" \
+  "$hook"
+
+# No reboot needed: systemd-sleep picks up every executable in system-sleep
+# the next time the machine suspends.

@@ -0,0 +1,170 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
+
+leaf="$ROOT/install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-suspend.sh"
+source_hook="$ROOT/default/systemd/system-sleep/rebind-brcmfmac"
+all="$ROOT/install/hardware/all.sh"
+migration="$ROOT/migrations/1789668939.sh"
+
+grep -q 'apple/fix-brcmfmac-suspend.sh' "$all" ||
+  fail "the brcmfmac suspend fix runs during hardware setup"
+pass "the brcmfmac suspend fix runs during hardware setup"
+
+# systemd-sleep runs every executable in system-sleep and silently skips
+# anything without the bit.
+[[ -x $source_hook ]] ||
+  fail "the hook source is executable"
+pass "the hook source is executable"
+
+test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT
+
+stub_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
+calls="$test_tmp/calls.log"
+hook="$test_tmp/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/rebind-brcmfmac"
+mkdir -p "$stub_bin" "$test_tmp/dmi" "$test_tmp/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep"
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/lspci" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+
+if (( ${T2_HARDWARE:-0} == 1 )); then
+  echo '01:00.0 Bridge [0680]: Apple Inc. T2 Security Chip [106b:1801]'
+fi
+if [[ -n ${WIFI_ID:-} ]]; then
+  echo "03:00.0 Network controller [0280]: Broadcom Inc. Wireless [14e4:$WIFI_ID]"
+fi
+for _ in {1..4096}; do
+  echo '02:00.0 Host bridge [0600]: Filler Device [ffff:0000]'
+done
+SH
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+
+printf 'sudo' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\t%s' "$@" >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\n' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+
+# install -o root -g root fails as the test user; ownership is already right
+# in the sandbox, so drop those flags before executing.
+args=()
+skip=0
+for arg in "$@"; do
+  if (( skip )); then
+    skip=0
+    continue
+  fi
+  case "$arg" in
+    -o|-g) skip=1 ;;
+    *) args+=("$arg") ;;
+  esac
+done
+"${args[@]}"
+SH
+
+chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*
+
+run_leaf() {
+  local vendor="$1" wifi_id="${2:-}" t2="${3:-0}"
+  rm -rf "$test_tmp/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep"
+  mkdir -p "$test_tmp/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep"
+  printf '%s' "$vendor" >"$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor"
+
+  local script="$test_tmp/leaf.sh"
+  sed -e "s|/sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor|$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor|g" \
+      -e "s|/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep|$test_tmp/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep|g" \
+      -e "s|\$OMARCHY_PATH|$ROOT|g" \
+      "$leaf" >"$script"
+
+  WIFI_ID="$wifi_id" T2_HARDWARE="$t2" PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" TEST_LOG="$calls" \
+    bash -eE -o pipefail -c 'source "$1"' bash "$script" </dev/null
+}
+
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 43a3 0 >/dev/null
+[[ -x $hook ]] ||
+  fail "a Mac with a BCM4350 gets the sleep hook" "$(ls -R "$test_tmp/usr" 2>&1)"
+cmp -s "$source_hook" "$hook" ||
+  fail "the installed hook matches the source"
+pass "a Mac with a BCM4350 gets the sleep hook"
+
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 4488 1 >/dev/null
+[[ -x $hook ]] ||
+  fail "a T2 Mac gets the sleep hook"
+pass "a T2 Mac gets the sleep hook"
+
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 43a0 0 >/dev/null
+[[ ! -e $hook ]] || fail "a Mac whose Wi-Fi brcmfmac does not drive is left alone"
+pass "a Mac whose Wi-Fi brcmfmac does not drive is left alone"
+
+run_leaf "LENOVO" 43a3 0 >/dev/null
+[[ ! -e $hook ]] || fail "non-Apple hardware is left alone"
+pass "non-Apple hardware is left alone"
+
+run_migration() {
+  local vendor="$1" wifi_id="${2:-}" t2="${3:-0}"
+  printf '%s' "$vendor" >"$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor"
+  : >"$calls"
+
+  WIFI_ID="$wifi_id" T2_HARDWARE="$t2" PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" TEST_LOG="$calls" \
+    OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" \
+    OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_DMI_VENDOR="$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor" \
+    OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_SLEEP_HOOK="$hook" \
+    bash -euo pipefail "$migration" >/dev/null
+}
+
+rm -f "$hook"
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 43a3 0
+[[ -x $hook ]] ||
+  fail "the migration installs the hook on a Mac that predates it"
+pass "the migration installs the hook on a Mac that predates it"
+
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 43a3 0
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "a repaired install is left untouched" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration is idempotent"
+
+printf '# local tweak\n' >> "$hook"
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 43a3 0
+cmp -s "$source_hook" "$hook" ||
+  fail "the migration refreshes a modified hook"
+pass "the migration refreshes a modified hook"
+
+rm -f "$hook"
+run_migration "LENOVO" 43a3 0
+[[ ! -e $hook ]] || fail "the migration skips non-Apple hardware"
+pass "the migration skips non-Apple hardware"
+
+# The hook itself: run it against a stub sysfs where unbind and bind are real
+# files, so the writes land and can be checked. /run is writable in tests.
+driver="$test_tmp/sys/bus/pci/drivers/brcmfmac"
+mkdir -p "$driver"
+ln -s "/sys/devices/pci0000:00/0000:02:00.0" "$driver/0000:02:00.0"
+touch "$driver/unbind" "$driver/bind"
+
+hook_script="$test_tmp/rebind-brcmfmac"
+sed "s|/sys/bus/pci/drivers/brcmfmac|$driver|g" "$source_hook" > "$hook_script"
+chmod +x "$hook_script"
+state_file="$test_tmp/state"
+export OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_SLEEP_STATE="$state_file"
+
+"$hook_script" pre
+grep -qx '0000:02:00.0' "$driver/unbind" ||
+  fail "pre-sleep unbinds the bound device" "$(cat "$driver/unbind")"
+[[ -f $state_file ]] || fail "pre-sleep records the unbound device"
+pass "pre-sleep unbinds the bound device"
+
+"$hook_script" post
+grep -qx '0000:02:00.0' "$driver/bind" ||
+  fail "post-sleep rebinds the same device" "$(cat "$driver/bind")"
+[[ ! -f $state_file ]] ||
+  fail "post-sleep clears the state file"
+pass "post-sleep rebinds the same device and clears state"
+
+# A post with no matching pre is a no-op, the case after a fresh boot.
+rm -f "$state_file"
+: > "$driver/bind"
+"$hook_script" post
+[[ ! -s $driver/bind ]] || fail "post without pre writes nothing"
+pass "post without pre is a no-op"

comments.body:
Related: #11434 is still open and targets the same brcmfmac firmware timeout on these Apple/Broadcom devices. The lifecycle differs: that PR unbinds/rebinds through a post-resume service, while this one unbinds before sleep and records which devices to rebind afterward.

These look like alternative fixes to coordinate before landing both migrations. A long-suspend test on the BCM4350 case here and the BCM43602 case in #11434 would help establish which lifecycle covers both reports.

Agreed these shouldn't both land — but I think the lifecycle difference settles it rather than test coverage alone. Unbinding pre-sleep means the firmware never executes its S3 suspend/resume path at all: the wedge is avoided, not recovered from. The post-resume service in #11434 still lets the firmware suspend normally and bets the rebind heals it afterward — which is exactly the assumption that fails in the long-suspend case here.

The hardware gate and device table are identical in both PRs, so this hook should cover the BCM43602 population as-is. @TheoAndersen — could you try the `system-sleep` hook from this PR on your MacBookPro11,5 instead of the resume service? Your lid-close repro is quick to run. If it fixes your case, I'd propose closing #11434 in favor of this one.
